findings.issue_text: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in app/models/optimized_image.rb; the second 3-arg definition (from, to, dimensions) silently replaces the 4-arg one (from, to, max_width, max_height), breaking existing callers with ArgumentError or misinterpreting max_height as opts

Non-admin users can push 10 MB images through uploads_controller; SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb no longer bounds anything server-side except the downsize loop, and the 10.megabytes cap only applies to the API URL path, making the effective limit hard-coded rather than admin-controlled

Downsize loop in uploads_controller resizes in place (tempfile.path as both source and destination) and never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, so a failed convert leaves a truncated/corrupt file that is passed to Upload.create_for as valid

tempfile.size is read after an external process rewrote the file in place, so the loop condition may be stale; the file may also still be oversized after 5 attempts yet is uploaded without re-checking the limit

Up to five synchronous ImageMagick convert invocations on a 10 MB image run inside the request cycle, blocking a worker for many seconds and creating a resource-exhaustion vector for any logged-in user

FileHelper.is_image?(filename) matches by extension, so non-images or SVGs with a .jpg name are passed to convert in place; allow_animation is gated on SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails (a thumbnail setting), so uploaded animated GIFs are flattened when that setting is off

Client-side check in utilities.js ignores file type, allowing non-image attachments up to 10 MB client-side while the server still rejects them at max_attachment_size_kb, giving a confusing server-side rejection instead of an immediate client error
The 413 alert in utilities.js reports a hard-coded 10240 KB regardless of the actual web-server body limit or site setting that triggered it, so the error message can state a wrong limit

No spec covers the new downsize path (oversized image reduced, convert failure, non-image with image extension, loop cap), and no spec updates cover the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/resize signatures

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Up to five synchronous ImageMagick convert invocations on a 10 MB image run inside the request cycle, blocking a worker for many seconds and creating a resource-exhaustion vector for any logged-in user

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that, for image uploads, runs up to 5 iterations of `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while the tempfile remains larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` ultimately executes ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with`, which is synchronous and blocks the Rails request thread/process until completion. Combined with raising the client-side and URL-download size limit to a hardcoded 10MB, a logged-in user can submit large images that trigger multiple convert runs inside the request cycle, creating a clear performance/resource-exhaustion risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FileHelper.is_image?(filename) matches by extension, so non-images or SVGs with a .jpg name are passed to convert in place; allow_animation is gated on SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails (a thumbnail setting), so uploaded animated GIFs are flattened when that setting is off

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows a new guard `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` before calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` and passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. The proposed finding hinges on unverified assumptions about `FileHelper.is_image?` (that it matches only by extension) and about how non-image/SVG content would be handled by the optimizer; none of that behavior is shown or changed in this diff. Likewise, using `allow_animated_thumbnails` to decide whether to preserve animation may be a product choice, but the diff does not establish that “flattening” is incorrect or unintended for uploads. Therefore the finding is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 413 alert in utilities.js reports a hard-coded 10240 KB regardless of the actual web-server body limit or site setting that triggered it, so the error message can state a wrong limit

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the 413 handler in `utilities.js` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` (10MB). A 413 (“entity too large”) can be triggered by whatever limit the server enforces (or by a different site setting), so the alert will always claim 10240 KB even when the actual configured/server limit differs. This is a verifiable correctness/usability issue introduced by the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new upload downsizing logic and changes `OptimizedImage` method signatures, but the proposed finding is about missing/unchanged specs. From the diff alone we cannot verify whether specs exist elsewhere or whether coverage is adequate; the diff simply doesn’t include any test changes. That makes the claim “No spec covers…” not a verifiable defect in this diff (it’s a process/coverage concern, not a concrete bug demonstrated here).
